h1: The 5 Best Full-Size Murphy Beds with Desks of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Full Murphy Beds with Desks: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 5 best full-size Murphy beds with desks of 2026, compared on mattress inclusion, storage, finish and price for small rooms.
mainKeyword: full size murphy bed with desk
summary: The AFI Northampton is the best full size Murphy bed with a desk, with a 6 inch memory foam mattress included in an assembled cabinet. The MERITLINE white cabinet is the budget route, the grey MERITLINE adds a bookcase, the Merax carries the most storage, and the THINK 30 is the style pick in walnut and gray.
intro: Murphy bed buyers tend to discover the mattress problem after the cabinet arrives. The frame closes against the wall with the bedding inside, so it can only take a mattress up to a certain thickness, and a standard full mattress is usually too deep. Plenty of cabinets ship without any mattress at all, which turns an apparent bargain into a bed plus a second purchase, usually a slim foam model.

So the first check is whether a mattress is included and what depth the cabinet accepts. Only five listings were genuine full size beds with a built-in desk, which is why this ranking has five picks, and review data on several of them is thin, which we flag. We compared mattress inclusion, storage, finish and price tier from the listings, with wall anchoring and clearance as the unglamorous checks every buyer must still make.

products.name: AFI Northampton Full Murphy Bed Desk with Memory Foam 6 Inch Mattress
products.verdict: The mattress is included, so the bed closes properly.
products.description:
The AFI Northampton earns first place by removing the mattress guess. It is a full size Murphy bed with a fold-down desk, a white finish and a 6 inch memory foam mattress included, sold as an assembled cabinet. A mattress sized for the frame means the bed closes the way the maker intended, and an assembled cabinet saves the hours that flat-pack cabinets cost.

The tradeoff is price. It sits in the $500 and up tier, well above the MERITLINE. Against the others, though, it is the only one that lists a mattress at all.

Buy it for a single purchase that covers bed, desk and bedding. The caveat is comfort: a 6 inch memory foam mattress is thin and firm, so heavier sleepers and regular overnight guests should weigh whether it suits them before relying on it as a daily bed.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a one box solution.

products.name: MERITLINE Full Murphy Bed with Desk, Wood Folding Hideaway Space Saving Wall Bed
products.verdict: The lowest priced confirmed full size desk combo.
products.description:
The white MERITLINE is the lowest-priced confirmed full size desk combo. It is a wood cabinet in white with a fold-down desk and a folding hideaway design, in the $200 to $500 tier. Wood construction gives it a firm, conventional look, and the desk drops down for work.

The price gap to the AFI is its whole argument, and that is why it lands second. The review base is thin and no mattress is listed as included, so expect to buy a slim one separately, and that adds to the real price.

Choose it for a solo sleeper on a budget who already owns or will buy a suitable slim mattress. The caveat is the unknown: confirm the mattress thickness the frame takes before ordering, because a mattress that is too deep prevents the bed from closing, and check assembly requirements.

products.name: MERITLINE Full Murphy Bed with Desk and Storage Shelves, Grey
products.verdict: Desk plus bookcase storage in a grey finish.
products.description:
The grey MERITLINE adds shelving to the same idea. It pairs a full size fold-down desk with storage shelves and a bookcase in a grey wood finish, in a hideaway wall bed design. For a room that doubles as an office and a guest room, the shelves hold books and supplies without taking extra floor space.

It ranks third because the added storage suits a room that needs it, but review data is limited and no price tier was available, while the white MERITLINE has a confirmed lower price. That missing price makes comparison harder.

Pick it if you want the desk and a bookcase in one footprint. The caveat is uncertainty: confirm the current price, ask about the mattress, and read the latest feedback, since limited data makes it a riskier buy than the AFI.

products.name: Merax Full Size Wall Murphy Bed with Desk, Top Cabinet and Storage Shelves
products.verdict: A top cabinet and shelves for the most storage.
products.description:
The Merax is the storage-heavy option. It is a full size wooden wall bed with a fold-down desk, a top cabinet and storage shelves, in the $500 and up tier. A top cabinet over the bed uses wall height that the others leave empty, which matters in a small room.

It ranks fourth because it holds the most storage, but it costs more than the MERITLINE and has a thin review record, so research current owner feedback closely. Against the AFI, it lists no mattress, so the true cost rises further.

Choose it for a small room that needs wall storage and a desk together. The caveat is weight and price: shelves and a top cabinet add load on the wall, so anchoring must be done properly, and you should confirm the mattress depth the frame allows.

products.name: THINK 30 Murphy Bed with Foldable Desk, Full Size, Walnut and Gray
products.verdict: A walnut and gray look with a separate desk hinge.
products.description:
The THINK 30 is the style pick. It is a full size cabinet with a foldable desk, a walnut and gray finish and a separate desk-fold hinge mechanism, in the $500 and up tier. A hinge dedicated to the desk keeps the work surface's fold separate from the bed's, which is a practical detail for daily use.

It ranks last because it costs as much as the AFI without a listed mattress, and review data is limited and middling. When a bed costs the same, the one that includes bedding is the better value.

Buy it if the finish is the deciding factor and you are happy to buy a slim mattress. The caveat is value: for the same tier, the AFI gives you a mattress and an assembled cabinet, so choose this only when the walnut and gray look is worth the difference.

whatMatters.detail: A Murphy bed closes with the mattress inside, so the frame limits thickness. A 6 inch memory foam mattress fits, but a 12 inch one may not. Check the maximum mattress depth in the specs, and be wary of listings that offer no figure, since that is the most common source of returns and awkward disputes with sellers.

A full bed needs floor space when open and ceiling height when closed. Measure the floor space it needs in use, plus the walkway around it, and check ceiling height against the cabinet. Clear the area at the foot so the bed can swing down without hitting furniture, and allow room to stand beside it.

A fold-down desk must be cleared before the bed opens, because items on it will slide or fall. Look for how the desk folds in the listing, and whether it has its own hinge, as the THINK 30 does. Plan a routine of clearing the surface before you open the bed, so a laptop never rides down with it.

A Murphy bed must be fixed to wall studs for safety, because the weight shifts as the bed opens. Check the hardware list in the listing and the manual, and never skip anchoring. If you rent, confirm your landlord allows wall anchoring, and ask whether drilling is acceptable before you hang anything on the wall.

Shelves and top cabinets add storage but also weight and cost, and they take away headroom above the bed. Choose what you will actually use, and compare the Merax and grey MERITLINE against a plain desk bed. Keep heavy items low so the cabinet stays balanced, and avoid overloading the top shelves.

faq.a: Only the AFI Northampton lists a 6 inch memory foam mattress. The MERITLINE, Merax and THINK 30 listings include none, so budget for a slim mattress that fits the frame, and confirm the maximum depth first.

Ignoring mattress thickness. A thick mattress may stop the bed from closing, so check the depth the cabinet accepts before you buy any mattress, even if it is a good one, since returns on bedding are awkward.

faq.q: Is the AFI worth it over the MERITLINE?
faq.a: If you need a mattress, yes. If you own a slim one, the white MERITLINE saves money, but its review base is thin, so check current feedback before ordering and ask about the mattress depth.
The AFI is sold as an assembled cabinet. The others may need assembly, so check the listing for details, and plan help for lifting the cabinet upright and fixing it to the wall studs.

Check the hinges and wall anchors periodically, and tighten any loose fasteners. Keep the mattress dry and the desk clear, and look for wear where the bed meets the floor or the wall, since a loose anchor is a safety risk.

faq.q: Can I leave things on the desk?
faq.a: No. Clear it before folding the bed, or items will fall. Keep a tidy routine, such as a small tray for the laptop and papers that you can move before opening the bed.

finalTake: Buy the AFI Northampton if you want bed, desk and mattress in one purchase, or the white MERITLINE if you own a slim mattress and need to save. The grey MERITLINE and Merax suit rooms that need shelving, and the THINK 30 is for buyers who choose on finish. Whatever you buy, anchor it to the studs.
